title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Sustainable Photocatalytic and Electrocatalytic HMF‐to‐FDCA Conversion: From Catalyst Engineering to Energy‐Saving Paired Electrolysis Systems
innovation: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic and electrocatalytic upgrading of lignocellulosic biomass into value‐added chemicals offers a sustainable route to carbon neutrality.
limitations: Descriptor transfer depends on whether the proposed active-site model remains physically faithful in MOF node or defect environments. Electronic-structure trends may be stronger than finite-temperature dynamics, solvent, or kinetics.
next_steps: Test whether active-site descriptors transfer to MOF nodes, defects, bimetallic sites, or local-field-controlled catalytic regimes. Test humid or multicomponent conditions and connect material metrics to process-level targets.
mof_relevance: Already in the MOF literature; keep it only if the method adds a new representation, label space, or uncertainty/active-learning angle.
mof_transfer_route: Use as direct MOF prior art or a benchmark for a more specific MOF task.

title: Assessing Structural, Thermal, and Mechanical Properties of Zirconium‐Based Metal‐Organic Frameworks via DFTB3 / 3OB MD Simulations: A Benchmark Beyond UiO Frameworks
innovation: The exceptional stability and broad application potential of zirconium-based metal-organic frameworks call for reliable atomistic methods capable of describing their structural, thermal, and mechanical properties.
limitations: Representation gains depend on whether periodicity, long-range electrostatics, and porous-framework topology are handled. Screening conclusions may depend on idealized structures, force fields, and missing defects/flexibility.
next_steps: Benchmark node/linker-aware periodic graphs against generic crystal representations on MOF properties.
mof_relevance: Already in the MOF literature; keep it only if the method adds a new representation, label space, or uncertainty/active-learning angle.
mof_transfer_route: Use as direct MOF prior art or a benchmark for a more specific MOF task.

title: Reliable methane storage screening and inverse design of metal organic frameworks under distribution shift
innovation: We study the methane deliverable (working) capacity across a public database of 252,353 frameworks described by 14 geometric and 148 chemical descriptors, with uptake from grand canonical Monte Carlo simulation at 5.8 and 65 bar.
limitations: Generative candidates may need explicit topology, charge-balance, and synthesizability constraints before MOF transfer. Screening conclusions may depend on idealized structures, force fields, and missing defects/flexibility.
next_steps: Recast the generator with MOF topology, linker-node compatibility, charge, and synthetic-accessibility constraints. Test humid or multicomponent conditions and connect material metrics to process-level targets.
